 Your Social Security COLA Notice Arrives in December. Here's How to Estimate Your 2027 Raise Before Then.
 Keith Speights, The Motley Fool 2026년 10월 25일 일 오전 9:04 UTC 0 Image source: Getty Images. Key Points
 The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6% COLA for 2027, the biggest raise for beneficiaries in four years.
 You can estimate your 2027 gross benefit using a simple calculation.
 Your take-home amount depends on 2027 Medicare Part B premiums, which will be announced in November.
 The $23,760 Social Security bonus most retirees completely overlook › 
 Social Security beneficiaries will receive their biggest raise in four years in 2027. The On Oct. 14, 2026, the Social Security Administration (SSA) announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for next year.
 SSA will send personalized notices to all beneficiaries that detail exactly what their new benefit payments will be, but those notices won't arrive until December. You could wait six weeks to find out how much you'll receive. However, you could also do the calculation yourself in under two minutes.

 An easy calculation and an even easier online tool
 If you want to know what your 2027 Social Security benefit will be before SSA's personalized notice comes in December, the math is simple. Just multiply your monthly gross benefit before any deductions by 1.036. The result will be your new monthly gross benefit for 2027 with the 3.6% COLA applied.
 For example, the average retiree's gross monthly benefit as of September 2026 was $2,088.79, based on SSA's monthly statistical snapshot. Multiplying that amount times 1.036 gives $2,163.99. The monthly increase equals $75.20, which is exactly 3.6% of the September average monthly benefit of $2,088.79.
 Keep in mind that those example numbers are only averages. Your projected Social Security benefit will likely be different, based on how much you earned over your career and when you claimed Social Security retirement benefits (if you claimed before your full retirement age , your benefits will be lower than they would otherwise be).
 Advertisement
 You don't have to perform this simple calculation to find out how the 2027 COLA will impact your Social Security benefits before the personalized notice arrives in the mail, though. The "my Social Security" account for most beneficiaries will display those personalized notices in late November before the mailed paper notices make it through the U.S. postal system. Just log into your account at SSA.gov. Then, navigate to the Message Center section to see the online notice. 
 A Medicare wildcard 
 Importantly, the numbers we have discussed are gross Social Security benefit amounts rather than the actual amount that will be deposited into your checking account. You won't be able to calculate this "take-home" amount yet. Why? The 2027 Medicare premiums haven't been finalized yet, and Medicare Part B premiums are deducted from most beneficiaries' Social Security payments.
 The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) will announce the 2027 premiums in November. In the meantime, retirees have reason to be optimistic. The 2026 Medicare Trustees Report, which was released in June, projected that the standard Part B premium would increase by around 3.25% next year. That's less than the Social Security COLA increase, which translates to good news for seniors. 
 The $23,760 Social Security bonus most retirees completely overlook
 If you're like most Americans, you're a few years (or more) behind on your retirement savings. But a handful of little-known "Social Security secrets" could help ensure a boost in your retirement income.
